circuit: copy of testcase/test31/test31.v (cone of n13[0]: 136 gates, depth 14, 57 NAND)
purpose: Basic single-turn queries over the CONE family. All four lines ask about the same cone, so only the chosen intent separates size, breakdown, one type, and depth.

lines.prompt: How much logic sits behind output n13[0]?
lines.why_correct: 'How much logic' is the gate count of the cone.
lines.why_hard: 'How much' is quantity-neutral -- it could equally be read as depth (14) or as a breakdown. Nothing in the sentence forces size.

lines.prompt: Break the logic behind n13[0] down by cell family for me.
lines.why_hard: count_gates answers with the same nine-type table for the WHOLE design -- a plausible-looking result with entirely different numbers. The net is named, so nothing has to be remembered; the risk is that the cone scope is simply not carried into the params.

lines.prompt: Within the logic behind n13[0], how many are NAND cells?
lines.why_hard: Dropping the scope still routes to count_type and still returns a number -- 3214 instead of 57. The intent looks right and only the params reveal the miss.

lines.prompt: How tall is the logic stack behind n13[0]?
lines.why_correct: 'How tall' is depth, scoped to this cone.
lines.why_hard: Mirrors line 3 on the same net: 136 vs 14. If lines 3 and 6 route to the same intent, one of them is wrong whichever it is.

lines.mechanism: sentence weight pulls to the design-wide reading
lines.why_hard: 'Taking the whole picture into account' sits in the focus position and pulls hard toward global_max_depth (58 here against the correct 14); the scope survives only in the trailing 'that ends up at n13[0]'. This is the phrasing shape that already beat the router on test83 line 5.
lines.prompt: Taking the whole picture into account, what is the longest run of gates that ends up at n13[0]?

notes: Values: cone_gate_count(n13[0])=136, cone_depth=14, NAND in cone=57, whole-design NAND=3214, breakdown nand:57 nor:35 or:5 not:12 dff:27.
Line 5 is scored on params: count_type without scope returns 3214 and still looks like a valid answer.
Lines 3 and 6 are a mirrored size/depth pair on the same net and must be scored together.

Every line is self-contained: nothing refers to an earlier turn. The agent sends no conversation history to the model (system = catalog, user = the current line only), so anaphoric wording would test dialogue memory rather than routing.
